chunks: He who assigns to Him (different) conditions does not believe in His oneness, nor does he who likens Him grasp His reality. He who illustrates Him does not signify Him. He who points at Him and imagines Him does not mean Him.
Everything that is known through itself has been created, and everything that exists by virtue of other things is the effect (of a cause).
He works but not with the help of instruments. He fixes measures but not with the activity of thinking. He is rich but not by acquisition.
ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the limits of human understanding of God's nature?
ai.summary: This passage from Imam Ali’s *Sermon of the Oneness of God* (Khutbat al-Tawhid) serves as a cornerstone of Shia theological discourse, distinguishing between *Tawhid al-Dhati* (Essential Oneness) and *Tawhid al-Sifati* (Attributes). It emphasizes *Dhat al-Ilah* (God's Essence) as incomprehensible to the human mind, rejecting *Tashbih* (anthropomorphism) and *Ta'til* (negation of attributes) by affirming that God is self-sufficient (*Al-Samad*) and uncreated, unlike all contingent beings.
